_meta.indication: CRESEMBA is an azole antifungal indicated for patients 18 years of age and older for the treatment of invasive aspergillosis and invasive mucormycosis

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, non-inferiority, multi-center trial comparing isavuconazonium to voriconazole
pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients with proven, probable, or possible invasive fungal infections (invasive aspergillosis) per EORTC/MSG 2008 criteria; patients with renal impairment (CrCl <50 mL/min) excluded
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Rate of all-cause mortality through Day 42 in the ITT population (non-inferiority margin 10%)
pivotal_trials.n: ITT population of 516 patients, 258 in each treatment group
pivotal_trials.result: All-cause mortality through Day 42 (ITT) was 18.6% isavuconazonium vs 20.2% voriconazole (treatment difference -1.0%, 95% CI -7.8%, 5.7%); non-inferiority demonstrated as the upper bound of the 95% CI was less than 10%

nct_ctgov.title: Isavuconazole (BAL8557) for Primary Treatment of Invasive Aspergillosis

pivotal_trials.design: Open-label, non-comparative trial; subset of patients with invasive mucormycosis
pivotal_trials.population: 37 patients with proven or probable invasive mucormycosis (EORTC/MSG-based criteria)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: All-cause mortality through Day 42 and overall response success at End-of-Treatment as assessed by the independent Data Review Committee
pivotal_trials.n: N=37 mucormycosis patients (21 primary, 11 refractory, 5 intolerant)
pivotal_trials.result: All-cause mortality through Day 42 was 14 (38%) overall; overall response success at End-of-Treatment was 11/35 (31%)

nct_ctgov.title: Isavuconazole in the Treatment of Renally Impaired Aspergillosis and Rare Fungi

key_safety: Most frequently reported adverse reactions: nausea (26%), vomiting (25%), diarrhea (22%), headache (17%), elevated liver chemistry tests (16%), hypokalemia (14%), constipation (13%), dyspnea (12%), cough (12%), peripheral edema (11%), back pain (10%). Warnings include hepatic adverse drug reactions, infusion-related reactions, hypersensitivity reactions, and embryo-fetal toxicity
target_moa: Isavuconazonium sulfate is the prodrug of isavuconazole, an azole antifungal that inhibits synthesis of ergosterol (a key component of the fungal cell membrane) via inhibition of cytochrome P-450 dependent lanosterol 14-alpha-demethylase, which converts lanosterol to ergosterol
modality: Small molecule (prodrug of isavuconazole, an azole antifungal)

rems.type: DRISK and DAIP concurred that a REMS is not required to ensure that the benefits of isavuconazonium outweigh the risks

advisory_committee.vote: Anti-Infective Drugs Advisory Committee (January 22, 2015): aspergillosis indication voted Yes 11, No 0, Abstain 0; mucormycosis indication voted Yes 8, No 2, Abstain 1

orphan_indication.text: Orphan drug designation for both indications (invasive aspergillosis and invasive mucormycosis)

citations.quote: As both products have orphan drug designation for both indications, pediatric studies under the Pediatric Research Equity Act (PREA) are not required.

basis.text: QIDP designation conferred priority review under GAIN (Title VIII of FDASIA)

citations.quote: As isavuconazonium sulfate has QIDP designation for the submitted indications, these NDAs received a priority review.

basis.text: Isavuconazonium designated a Qualified Infectious Disease Product (QIDP) for invasive aspergillosis (Nov 8, 2013) and invasive mucormycosis (Feb 14, 2014), eligible for five additional years of marketing exclusivity under GAIN

citations.quote: November 8, 2013: Isavuconazonium designated as a Qualified Infectious Disease Product (QIDP) for the indication of treatment of invasive aspergillosis
February 14, 2014: Isavuconazonium designated as a QIDP for the indication of treatment of invasive mucormycosis.
These NDAs are eligible for five additional years of marketing exclusivity under GAIN.

summary.text: Isavuconazonium sulfate (CRESEMBA) received QIDP designation under GAIN, which conferred priority review, and had orphan drug designation for both indications; it was reviewed by the Anti-Infective Drugs Advisory Committee on January 22, 2015 and approved via traditional approval (not accelerated approval)

citations.quote: As isavuconazonium sulfate has QIDP designation for the submitted indications, these NDAs received a priority review.
As both products have orphan drug designation for both indications, pediatric studies under the Pediatric Research Equity Act (PREA) are not required.
These NDAs were discussed by the Anti-Infective Drugs Advisory Committee on January 22, 2015.
